correctness.rationale: Averaging an ergodic time-t MME over one time interval produces a flow-invariant measure; entropy affinity and time scaling make it a flow MME, and a flow-invariant set is also time-t invariant, so the average is flow-ergodic. Uniqueness of ergodic decomposition then identifies the original measure with a time-t component of one of the finitely many flow MMEs. In the Bernoulli-times-rotation model, irrational t/c gives an ergodic rotation and hence an ergodic product with the weakly mixing Bernoulli time map; rational p/q decomposes Haar measure into continuum many uniform q-cycle measures, each producing an ergodic product of the same maximal entropy. Zang's full-text Lemma 7.5 independently confirms the component-averaging mechanism in the time-one case.
correctness.risk: The conclusion inherits Zang's nonsingular C-infinity three-dimensional hypotheses and assumes the measured-flow period supplied by the Ledrappier--Lima--Sarig classification.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact structural boundary for whether flow-level finiteness survives time discretization: generic times preserve the finite family, while a simple arithmetic resonance causes an immediate jump to continuum multiplicity. This is a natural dynamical consequence of recent finiteness theory and a useful all-time classification.

final_claim: For a nonsingular \(C^\infty\) positive-entropy flow on a compact three-manifold with finitely many ergodic flow MMEs \(\mu_i\), each Bernoulli or Bernoulli times a rotation of period \(c_i\), every ergodic MME of \(\varphi^t\) is a time-t component of some \(\mu_i\). Thus nonresonant \(t\) gives exactly the original finite family, while any rational resonance \(t/c_i\in\mathbb Q\) gives continuum many ergodic time-map MMEs.
limitations: The theorem concerns ergodic MMEs, not lower-entropy invariant measures or general equilibrium states.
It does not provide an effective algorithm for the periods \(c_i\).
